_about: RQ3 section strings and numbers, built by docs/launch_20261116/tools/build_rq3_data.py from the paper's figure data; do not edit by hand. Paper text is {t, src}; `edits` lists every change to a paper sentence; `numbers` gives each displayed number's data file and the paper file that prints it. Tiles stand for counts, not individual texts: no reviewer, username or per-review result is included. Every string that is not paper text is in `ui` (labels and controls), `demo` (the one illustrative example: a synthetic review, written for this page; the answer's name is the placeholder John Doe, never a real name) or `notes` without a `src` (the section's footnotes; a note with `src` is paper text).

takeaway.t: Frontier models can name the person who wrote a text

context.t: We provide no tools, web access, or candidate lists.

steps.t: Naming the person behind a human-written text is an open-world task with countless possible outputs.
Given a single text, models return the human author's name, a list of supporting observations, and a confidence level.
Claude Fable 5.2 names the reviewer of 55% of 15K anonymous ICML 2020 reviews whose content and authorship were never made public (studied with IRB approval).
Fable 5.2, the best performing model in all domains, exhibits considerable gains over Opus 5.5, which was released less than two months prior.
Given the list of about 4K ICML 2020 reviewers, Fable 5.2 names the reviewer of 76% of 2K of these reviews, out of a possible 84%.

steps.t: On texts published after its training cutoff, it also names the reviewer of 78% of Nature journal reviews, the writer of all 15 stories by authors with >1M Goodreads ratings, at least one author of 46% of arXiv papers, and the username behind 69% of comments made by active Redditors.

head.t: Confident answers are almost always right.

steps.t: When Fable 5.2's confidence is 25% or more (25% of responses), its predictions are 87% correct.
Generally, the explanations cover both the text's content as well as its writing style.

demo.t: The paper proposes a simple regularizer for training under label noise and reports gains on three image benchmarks.
The idea is easy to follow, and the experiments are thorough.
It is unclear whether the gains come from the regularizer or from extra tuning. Results over more random seeds would help.

notes.t: Illustrative example, written for this page: not a real review.
The name shown is a placeholder.
We report only aggregate results and do not reveal any text from individual peer reviews or reviewer identities.
On private peer reviews, Fable 5.2 leads with 56% accuracy, while on public reviews from the Nature journal family it reaches 78%.
Fable 5.2 identifies 4% of stories by authors without a Goodreads profile, 50% by those with 1k–10k ratings, and 100% by authors with over 10k ratings.
Claude Fable 5.2's attribution accuracy rises from 2% for inactive users to 13% for those with 1–50 posts, reaching 69% for users with over 500 posts.
